paragraphs: Hyman describes Bar Lofayni as very wealthy. In Esther Rabbah 2:3, when Bar Lofayni married off his daughter from Tzippori to Acco, he set up wine-serving shops all along the route, with golden lamps on both sides.

notes.text: The Esther Rabbah locator פ״כ-ג remains unresolved; the route, wine-serving shops and golden lamps are retained in full.

The saved whole Torat Emet EstherRabbah2 scalar2 explicitly names Bar Lofayni, his daughter’s Tzippori-to-Acco wedding route, wine-serving shops and golden lamps on both sides. The match is2:3 alongside supplied פ״כ-ג, not proof that a printed כ was substituted for ב. The body’s subject comes from the heading and is supported by that named occurrence; no omitted narrative is added and the earlier bounded nonmatch is not erased.

Hyman’s printed volume I, p. 286, reads פ״ב-ג, chapter 2, section 3. The supplied Hebrew transcription instead has פ״כ-ג. Esther Rabbah 2:3 names Bar Lofayni and recounts the Tzippori-to-Acco wedding route, wine-serving shops and golden lamps on both sides. The express description of his wealth is Hyman’s.
